property_summary: For any deployed C, calling currentVersion() returns the oracle().currentVersion() with its price transformed by the product's payoffDefinition (i.e. returned.price == payoffDefinition.transform(oracle.currentVersion().price)); the mutant that returns oracle.currentVersion() directly will break this when the payoffDefinition changes the price (some oracle price where transform(price) != price).

For any oracle version returned by the product, the product's currentVersion() always returns the oracle version with its price transformed by the product's payoffDefinition; the mutant that returns the oracle's raw currentVersion() will sometimes return a different price when the payoffDefinition actually changes the price.

For every oracle price, C.currentVersion() returns the oracle's version but with its price transformed by the product's payoffDefinition; the mutant returns the raw oracle version (no transform), so when payoffDefinition.transform(price) != price the mutant's return differs.

For every oracle currentVersion returned by the product's oracle, C.currentVersion() returns that version with its price transformed by the product's payoffDefinition; the mutant that returns oracle().currentVersion() directly will sometimes return a different price when payoffDefinition.transform(price) != price.

For every oracle price input, C.currentVersion() returns the oracle's currentVersion with its price transformed by the product's payoffDefinition; the mutant that returns oracle().currentVersion() directly can return an untransformed price when transform(price) != price, so there exists some oracle price for which the mutant's returned price differs.

For any oracle state, C.currentVersion() returns the oracle's currentVersion with the same timestamp (reference preserves timestamp), whereas the mutant increments the returned timestamp by 1 and thus can return a different timestamp for some oracle states.

For any oracle-provided version returned by C.currentVersion(), the returned OracleVersion.timestamp equals the oracle's currentVersion().timestamp (reference preserves timestamp for all inputs); the mutant increments the returned timestamp by 1 and therefore will produce a different timestamp for some oracle states.

For any oracle state, calling C.currentVersion() returns an OracleVersion whose timestamp equals the oracle's currentVersion().timestamp (reference preserves the oracle timestamp; the mutant increments the returned timestamp by 1 and thus violates equality for some oracle states).

For any oracle state, C.currentVersion() returns an OracleVersion whose timestamp equals the underlying oracle().currentVersion().timestamp; the mutant increments the returned timestamp by 1 and thus violates this equality for some oracle timestamps.

For any deployed oracle contract, C.currentVersion() returns an OracleVersion whose timestamp is equal to the oracle's currentVersion().timestamp; the mutant increments the returned timestamp by 1 so for some oracle timestamps the equality is broken.

For any oracleVersion input, C.atVersion(uint256) returns an OracleVersion whose price field equals the transformed price (payoffDefinition.transform applied to the underlying oracle().atVersion), while the mutant returns the raw oracle price unchanged—so there exists some oracleVersion where those prices differ and the mutant fails.

For any oracleVersion id, C.atVersion(id) returns an OracleVersion whose price equals payoffDefinition().transform(oracle().atVersion(id).price); the mutant that returns oracle().atVersion(id) directly will produce a different price for some inputs, so there exists an oracleVersion where the returned price differs.

For any oracleVersion id, C.atVersion(id) always returns an OracleVersion whose price has been transformed by the product's payoffDefinition (i.e. equals payoffDefinition().transform(oracle().atVersion(id).price)); the mutant that forwards oracle().atVersion(id) without transforming can return a different price for some oracleVersion ids.

For every oracleVersion id, the reference C.atVersion(id) returns an OracleVersion whose price equals the payoffDefinition-transformed price produced by the configured oracle (i.e. c.atVersion(id).price == c.payoffDefinition().transform(oracle.atVersion(id).price)); the mutant that simply returns oracle().atVersion(id) can return a different price for some oracleVersion inputs, so the property (returned price equals transformed underlying oracle price) will hold for the reference for all inputs and fail for some input on the mutant.

For every oracleVersion id, C.atVersion(id) returns an OracleVersion whose price equals the payoffDefinition-transformed price of the configured oracle; the mutant that returns the raw oracle value without transforming will for some oracleVersion return a different price, violating this rule.

For any stored maker fee value, the contract's makerFee() getter returns exactly that stored value; the mutant multiplies the stored value by 2 so it will return a different value for some fuzzed stored fees.

For any stored maker fee value in the product, the public getter makerFee() returns exactly the stored maker fee; the mutant doubles the returned value for some stored fees, so for some fuzzed maker fee values the returned value will differ (reference: equality holds for all inputs; mutant: inequality for some inputs).
